conditions.workerPolicy: one fresh Dedicated Worker per run
conditions.repeatPolicy: Phase 2-C2.5-B rule, unchanged (as D2-b): a context whose attempt 1 pair had a page / browser crash, a native Worker failure, a mode disagreement or a CDP attach failure is run once more (at most 2 attempts); both attempts are kept
conditions.classificationPolicy: Phase 2-C2.5-B pre-registered rule, unchanged (phase2c25bPairClassification, as D2-b); an explicit V8 OOM crash key is auxiliary only; the summary browser_no_failure_all_selected_contexts is added beside it
conditions.nodeParityPolicy: Every context ended normally in Node D2-d, so every Browser normal run must equal Node D2-d in status, Search summary, first Candidate key, extent / exhaustion, and (instrumented) prediction counts and final progress (Gogma max depth, cumulative generated / frontier, max generated per depth and its depth, Skill max depth / states, settled work)
conditions.formalSeriesPolicy: validatePhase2C25D2BFormalSeries() (the D2-b validator, reused unchanged): every workload context has exactly one attempt 1 minimal / instrumented run; the repeat decision recomputed by phase2c25bRepeatDecision() equals the recorded one; exactly one attempt 2 pair where it repeats and none otherwise; no attempt above 2, foreign context, duplicate run or extra / missing decision; driver modes exactly minimal + instrumented, allowRepeat true, only null, completedAt present. Checked before the analysis; a failure ends the analyzer without a result.

formal: Context parity: before any Search, every page session re-derived the workload orientations from the original Export and matched the Phase 2-C2.5-A evidence field by field (digests included); the workload equals the D2-d RESULT workloadSelection.

Formal Browser classification per context (Phase 2-C2.5-B / D2-b rule, unchanged): c0-p0#0 browser_no_failure (D2-b before: browser_no_failure); c12-p0#0 browser_no_failure (D2-b before: inconclusive_page_or_browser_crash); c2-p1#0 browser_no_failure (D2-b before: inconclusive_page_or_browser_crash); c8-p1#0 browser_no_failure (D2-b before: browser_no_failure); c13-p4#0 browser_no_failure (D2-b before: browser_no_failure). Representative verdict: not_reproduced. Summary: browser_no_failure_all_selected_contexts.

After H1, c12-p0#0 no longer reproduced the D2-b renderer loss in the Chrome Dedicated Worker: both modes ended stopped_by_extent_before_candidate, equal to Node D2-d in status, Search summary, first Candidate key, extent / exhaustion, instrumented prediction counts and instrumented final progress.

After H1, c2-p1#0 no longer reproduced the D2-b renderer loss in the Chrome Dedicated Worker: both modes ended first_candidate, equal to Node D2-d in status, Search summary, first Candidate key, extent / exhaustion, instrumented prediction counts and instrumented final progress.
In the 5 measured contexts, every H1-after Chrome Dedicated Worker Search-only run ended normally, and its Candidate-visible semantics equalled Node D2-d.

notYet: That the Global Planner memory problem is solved: only the Search-only run of these contexts was measured, not the Global Planner kernel (portfolio, trials, full runs), the other Phase 2-C2 OOM orientations, other browsers or devices.

A memory-efficiency multiple from the CDP samples: they are sampled (about 500 ms), include uncollected garbage, depend on GC timing, and runs end at different points (a lost run is cut at the loss); the before / after values describe what was observed, not bytes per state.

The Dedicated Worker's own heap limit. Heap measurement boundary: the Dedicated Worker used heap sampled by CDP reached 0.62-2.21 GiB (per-run sampled maxima) in the primary runs (normal terminations and losses alike); the page realm reported performance.memory.jsHeapSizeLimit 4395630592 bytes (about 4.09 GiB), a value of another realm given for reference only; the Dedicated Worker realm did not expose its own jsHeapSizeLimit, so the Worker's actual heap limit was not measured (unknown) and is not taken to equal the page realm value. Neither value is compared directly with the Node 8 GB heap limit.
A heap comparison with Node D2-d: Node heap bytes and limits are not compared with the Browser (different runtimes; the sampled Browser maximum over all runs was 2.21 GiB).
A Browser / Node speed ratio: one run per mode and attempt only.
